AI.title_translation: 语义触及对象选择却未能完成任务：VLA在何处易受地标同义词的影响？
AI.tldr: VLA模型对地标同义词指令非常脆弱，语义能引导对象选择但影响任务完成度，而通过微调VLM与动作生成器之间的连接器可以有效修复这一缺陷。
AI.motivation: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略对指令重写非常脆弱，而现有的成功率指标无法区分策略是在选择对象时失败还是在完成任务时失败，也无法指出应在策略的何处进行干预。
AI.method: 研究了已发布的GR00T N1.7模型在LIBERO-Spatial任务上的表现，分析了视觉-语言模型（VLM）与动作生成器连接器前后的特征替换（pasting）、遮挡以及针对多样化地标词的微调方法。
AI.result: 同义词会误导策略选择错误的碗，但仍能完成部分任务；在连接器前替换地标词向量几乎总能改变选择，而在连接器后需要组合多个标记才能改变选择；仅在多样化地标词上微调连接器即可有效修复同义词带来的性能缺陷。
AI.conclusion: VLA策略对地标同义词的鲁棒性不足主要源于连接器前后的表征差异。通过对连接器进行多样化地标指令微调，可以有效修复策略漏洞，提升模型在闭环交互中的鲁棒性。
AI.translation: VLA策略对指令重写非常脆弱。单纯的成功率无法说明策略是没有选择对象还是没有完成任务，也无法说明应该在策略的哪个位置进行干预。我们研究了已发布的GR00T N1.7模型在两个LIBERO-Spatial任务上的表现，这两个任务仅在地标词（指示要拿两个碗中的哪一个）上有差异。与虚构词不同，训练指令中没有出现的同义词会将策略引向它们所命名的碗，但在一个任务的闭环剧集中完成了67.6%，而原始词则为100%。在视觉-语言模型与动作生成器之间的连接器之前，仅将地标标记的向量替换为另一个地标的向量（粘贴）几乎会将每个剧集都导向另一个碗。在连接器之后，在地标、剩余指令或图像标记处单独进行粘贴很少能改变选择，但任何两者结合都可以。在连接器之后向动作生成器隐藏地标标记，仍然会降低表现不佳的同义词的任务完成度。针对多样化地标词进行微调可以修复该任务中对未出现在微调中的同义词的任务完成度；而针对原始指令进行微调则不能。仅在多样化词汇上训练连接器就足够了，将在这些词汇上完全微调的策略的连接器复制到在原始指令上微调的策略中也同样有效。起始帧的开环评分漏掉了连接器外部的权重也承担了部分修复工作这一事实。目前，基于这些证据，对重写鲁棒性的评估应该在执行了动作的闭环中进行，对连接器的两侧进行干预，并分别对外在选择和任务完成度进行评分。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了VLA策略对地标同义词重写的脆弱性，发现语义能够触及对象选择但未必能完成任务。通过对VLM与动作生成器连接前后的干预分析及连接器微调实验，证明了应在闭环中评估重写鲁棒性，并通过多样化微调连接器修复漏洞。
AI.keywords: VLA, 语言重写, 鲁棒性, 连接器, 具身智能
AI.comments: 该论文揭示了VLA模型对语言重写（如近义词）的脆弱性，深入剖析了VLM与动作生成器连接前后的表征机制，并提出了通过微调连接器来增强鲁棒性的有效方法。研究方法严谨且洞察深刻，对具身大模型的发展具有重要参考价值。

title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
comments: 8-page main paper with references and supplementary material (15 pages); 5 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI Project page: https://starsholic.github.io/AeroRSI/
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.
comment: 8-page main paper with references and supplementary material (15 pages); 5 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI Project page: https://starsholic.github.io/AeroRSI/

AI.title_translation: AeroRSI：用于空中视觉语言导航的递归自我改进
AI.tldr: AeroRSI是一个针对无人机视觉语言导航的递归自我改进框架，通过让策略自我评估修复效果并进行迭代学习，在无需额外人工标注的情况下显著提升了导航成功率并减少了碰撞。
AI.motivation: 视觉语言动作（VLA）模型虽然使无人机能够听从自然语言指令，但在闭环飞行中仍然频频失败。纠正这些失败需要修复动作，但人类飞行员无法大规模标注，规则基础的规划器也无法可靠提供，因此需要一种使 aerial 导航策略能够从自身失败中迭代学习的框架。
AI.method: 提出了AeroRSI递归自我改进框架，核心思想是让失效的策略通过从修复点继续飞行来自我判断修复效果，将采样的动作或规则提案转化为可靠的监督信号，并在每一轮中更新监督、锚定当前策略的失败、通过延续验证修复并进行蒸馏。
AI.result: 在TravelUAV数据集上，经过三轮迭代，一个2B参数的有监督策略的成功率从46.4%提高到67.5%，碰撞率减少了一半，比相同初始化下的先前技术水平提升了10.6个百分点，且无需额外的人工标注或推理成本。
AI.conclusion: AeroRSI通过递归自我改进机制，有效提升了无人机在视觉语言导航任务中的性能，显著降低了碰撞率，为解决VLA模型在闭环飞行中的失败问题提供了一种可扩展且高效的无监督方案。
AI.translation: 视觉语言动作（VLA）模型使无人机（UAV）能够遵循自然语言指令，但在闭环飞行中仍然频繁失败。纠正这些失败需要修复，即在策略本身到达的状态下避免失败的动作，人类飞行员无法大规模标注这些动作，规则基础的规划器也无法可靠地提供。在本文中，我们提出了AeroRSI，这是一个递归自我改进框架，其中空中导航策略从自身的失败中迭代学习。我们的核心观点是，失败的策略应该通过从修复点继续飞行来判断自身的通过修复。以这种方式判断，其采样的动作甚至直接模仿时会损害策略的规则基础提案，都变成了可靠的监督。此外，一个回合在其第一次失败时终止，在修复早期的失败之前隐藏后续的失败。因此，AeroRSI在每一轮中更新其监督，锚定当前策略的失败，通过其延续验证修复，并在保持其他地方行为的同时对其进行蒸馏。在TravelUAV上，经过三轮迭代，一个有监督的2B参数策略的成功率从46.4%提高到67.5%，碰撞率减少了一半，在相同的初始化下，超越了以前的技术水平10.6个百分点，且没有额外的人类标签或推理成本。代码和模型可在 https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI 获取。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了AeroRSI，这是一个用于空中视觉语言导航的递归自我改进框架。该框架允许无人机导航策略通过让失败的策略评估自身的修复效果（通过继续飞行）来从自身失败中学习，从而在不需要额外人类标签的情况下，显著提高导航成功率并减少碰撞。
AI.keywords: Vision-Language Navigation, Recursive Self-Improvement, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, Policy Learning
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的递归自我改进框架（AeroRSI），专门用于解决无人机视觉语言导航中闭环飞行失败率高的问题。其核心创新在于让策略通过“继续飞行”来自我评估修复效果，从而将原本有缺陷的动作或规则提案转化为可靠的监督信号。这种方法无需额外的人工标注或增加推理成本，大幅提升了导航成功率并减少了碰撞，具有很高的实用价值和学术意义。

title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
summary: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. The resulting adaptive temporal partitions guide frame budget allocation based on query relevance and temporal extent, enabling informative frame selection under limited visual budgets. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that APS consistently improves performance across diverse LVLM backbones, achieving the highest average gains over uniform sampling among competing methods. Further analyses validate the effectiveness of adaptive partitioning and demonstrate its generalizability across model scales, similarity encoders, and advanced LVLMs.

AI.title_translation: APS：基于自适应分区的长视频理解帧选择方法
AI.tldr: 提出了一种无需训练的自适应时间分区帧选择框架（APS），通过动态优化分区和预算分配，显著提升了大语言模型处理长视频的效率与性能。
AI.motivation: 现有基于区域的帧选择方法通常依赖于固定或预定义的时间分区，容易导致次优的时间区域，从而影响后续的预算分配和帧选择效果。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为APS的训练免费框架，将时间分区表述为复杂度正则化的拟合问题，并通过动态规划联合优化分区边界和局部模型。
AI.result: 在Video-MME、MLVU和LongVideoBench上的大量实验表明，APS在各种LVLM骨干网上持续提升了性能，并在竞争方法中实现了对均匀采样最高的平均性能增益。
AI.conclusion: APS通过自适应时间分区和预算分配，有效解决了长视频理解中的高计算成本与信息丢失之间的矛盾，在多个基准测试中展现出卓越的性能与泛化能力。
AI.translation: 大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）的最新进展显著提高了视频理解能力，然而由于大量视觉输入的巨大计算成本，处理长视频仍然具有挑战性。帧选择提供了一种高效的替代方案，但许多现有的基于区域的方法依赖于固定或预定义的时间分区，这可能导致次优的时间区域，从而损害后续的预算分配和帧选择。在这项工作中，我们提出了基于自适应分区的帧选择（APS），这是一个无需训练的框架，它将时间分区调整为查询-帧相关性的局部变化。具体而言，APS将时间分区表述为一个复杂度正则化的拟合问题，通过动态规划共同优化分区边界和局部模型。由此产生的自适应时间分区根据查询相关性和时间范围指导帧预算分配，在有限的视觉预算下实现信息丰富的帧选择。在Video-MME、MLVU和LongVideoBench上的大量实验表明，APS在不同的LVLM骨干网中持续改善了性能，在竞争方法中实现了对均匀采样的最高平均增益。进一步的分析验证了自适应分区的有效性，并证明了其在模型规模、相似度编码器和高级LVLM中的通用性。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了APS（Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection）框架，这是一种用于长视频理解的无需训练的方法。它通过动态规划自适应地将时间划分为不同的区域，根据查询相关性优化帧预算分配，从而在有限的视觉输入下显著提升大视觉语言模型的性能。
AI.keywords: 长视频理解, 大视觉语言模型, 自适应分区, 帧选择, 动态规划
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种无需训练的自适应分区帧选择框架（APS），通过动态规划解决长视频理解中由于计算成本高昂而面临的冗余帧问题。其创新点在于将时间分区建模为复杂度正则化的拟合问题，能够根据查询-帧相关性的局部变化动态调整分区边界，从而在有限的视觉预算下显著提升大视觉语言模型（LVLMs）的性能。局限性方面，抽象中未明确提及。

title: CausalDrive: Causal Decomposition for Data-Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Efficient use of expert demonstrations is essential for end-to-end autonomous driving. However, directly imitating expert trajectories couples nominal intention, which specifies where the vehicle should go, with multimodal driving styles, which determine how that intention is executed. Different combinations of these factors can yield similar expert trajectories, obscuring their respective causal contributions and forcing the policy to learn both from a single entangled target. This ambiguity limits how effectively the policy can exploit expert demonstrations. We propose CausalDrive, a causal decomposition framework for data-efficient driving policy learning that separates deterministic nominal intention prediction from probabilistic driving style modeling. Specifically, we construct counterfactual nominal trajectories from navigation command, map topology, and ego state by removing style dependent effects, providing a Nominal Intention Planner with supervision independent of expert trajectories. Conditioned on the predicted nominal intention and surrounding agents, a diffusion-based Style Execution Policy models diverse driving styles as a multimodal distribution over residuals between nominal and expert trajectories. This causally structured supervision reduces redundant learning of shared nominal behavior in routine scenarios, directing expert supervision toward informative execution variations and improving data utilization. CausalDrive achieves 91.2 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 89.5 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, matching or surpassing state-of-the-art performance. Further experiments demonstrate strong performance with limited expert data and clear advantages in challenging interactive scenarios.

AI.title_translation: CausalDrive：用于数据高效端到端自动驾驶的因果分解
AI.tldr: CausalDrive通过将行驶意图与驾驶风格进行因果解耦，显著提升了端到端自动驾驶的数据利用率和性能。
AI.motivation: 直接模仿专家轨迹将名义意图与多模态驾驶风格耦合在一起，导致因果贡献模糊，迫使策略从单一纠缠的目标中学习，从而限制了专家演示的利用效率。
AI.method: 提出了CausalDrive框架，分离确定性的名义意图预测（使用导航命令、地图拓扑和自车状态构建反事实名义轨迹）与概率驱动风格建模（基于扩散模型建模名义轨迹与专家轨迹之间的残差）。
AI.result: 在NAVSIM v1上达到了91.2 PDMS，在NAVSIM v2上达到了89.5 EPDMS，达到或超越了最先进的性能，并在有限的专家数据和复杂的交互场景中表现出优势。
AI.conclusion: CausalDrive通过将名义意图预测与概率驾驶风格建模进行因果分解，有效提高了端到端自动驾驶对专家演示的数据利用效率，在NAVSIM上取得了SOTA的性能。
AI.translation: 高效利用专家示范对于端到端自动驾驶至关重要。然而，直接模仿专家轨迹将指定车辆去向的名义意图与决定该意图如何执行的多模态驾驶风格耦合在了一起。这些因素的不同组合可以产生相似的专家轨迹，掩盖了它们各自的因果贡献，并迫使策略从单一纠缠的目标中学习这两者。这种模糊性限制了策略有效利用专家示范的能力。我们提出了CausalDrive，这是一个用于数据高效驾驶策略学习的因果分解框架，它将确定性的名义意图预测与概率驾驶风格建模分离。具体来说，我们通过去除风格依赖的影响，从导航命令、地图拓扑和自车状态构建反事实名义轨迹，为名义意图规划器提供独立于专家轨迹的监督。以预测的名义意图和周围智能体为条件，基于扩散的风格执行政策将多样化的驾驶风格建模为名义轨迹与专家轨迹之间残差的多模态分布。这种具有因果结构的监督减少了常规场景下对共享名义行为的冗余学习，将专家监督引导至信息丰富的执行变化中，并提高了数据利用率。CausalDrive在NAVSIM v1上实现了91.2的PDMS，在NAVSIM v2上实现了89.5的EPDMS，达到或超越了最先进的性能。进一步的实验证明了其在有限专家数据下的强劲性能以及在具有挑战性的交互场景中的明显优势。
AI.summary: CausalDrive是一个用于数据高效自动驾驶策略学习的因果分解框架。它将确定性的名义意图预测与基于扩散模型的概率驾驶风格建模相分离，减少了常规场景下共享名义行为的冗余学习，将专家监督引导至信息丰富的执行变化，从而显著提高了数据利用效率和模型性能。
AI.keywords: 端到端自动驾驶, 因果分解, 数据效率, 模仿学习, 扩散模型
AI.comments: CausalDrive引入了因果分解的思想，将名义意图（去哪儿）与驾驶风格（怎么去）解耦，这有效地解决了端到端自动驾驶中模仿学习的混淆问题，极大地提升了数据利用率和在复杂交互场景下的性能。

title: Learning Where and How Much to Sample: Volume-Adaptive k-Space Acquisition for Accelerated MRI
summary: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential medical imaging technique, but its high costs and long acquisition times can limit accessibility. Accelerated MRI reduces acquisition time through k-space undersampling, yet conventional methods often rely on predefined sampling patterns and uniform slice budgets, overlooking anatomical variations and inter-slice relationships. In this paper, we propose a volume-adaptive k-space acquisition framework that jointly learns where and how much to sample across an entire MRI volume. Using only acquired auto-calibration signal (ACS) measurements, our method exploits volume-wide anatomical information to adaptively allocate sampling budgets across slices while identifying informative k-space lines. A learned joint slice--frequency refinement module coordinates sampling decisions while preserving an exact total volume-level acquisition budget. To reconstruct the acquired measurements, we design a sensitivity-aware synchronous cross-slice reconstruction network that estimates coil sensitivities from ACS measurements and progressively refines neighboring-slice reconstructions while enforcing hard k-space data consistency. Both networks are jointly optimized using reconstruction-based supervision without requiring fully sampled k-space at inference. Experiments on knee and brain MRI across multiple contrasts and acceleration factors demonstrate the adaptive behavior of our acquisition framework and evaluate its reconstruction performance.

AI.title_translation: 学习在哪里以及采样多少：用于加速MRI的体积自适应k空间采集
AI.tldr: 提出一种体积自适应k空间采集框架，通过学习在哪里以及采样多少来加速MRI，并用一个同步交叉切片重建网络进行图像重建。
AI.motivation: 磁共振成像(MRI)成本高、采集时间长，且现有加速MRI方法依赖预定义采样模式和统一切片预算，忽略了解剖变异和切片间关系。
AI.method: 提出一个体积自适应k空间采集框架，它联合学习在整个MRI体积中在哪里以及采样多少。该方法仅使用ACS测量，利用体积范围内的解剖信息自适应分配切片采样预算并识别信息丰富的k空间线。一个学习到的联合切片-频率细化模块协调采样决策。同时，设计了一个敏感度感知的同步交叉切片重建网络，从ACS测量估计线圈敏感度，并逐步细化相邻切片重建。采集和重建网络通过基于重建的监督联合优化。
AI.result: 在膝盖和大脑MRI（多种对比度和加速因子）上的实验证明了该采集框架的自适应行为，并评估了其重建性能。
AI.conclusion: 该体积自适应k空间采集框架及其重建网络能够有效地加速MRI，并表现出良好的自适应采样和重建性能。
AI.translation: 磁共振成像(MRI)是一种重要的医学成像技术，但其高成本和长采集时间可能会限制可及性。加速MRI通过k空间欠采样来减少采集时间，但传统方法通常依赖预定义的采样模式和统一的切片预算，忽略了解剖变异和切片间关系。在本文中，我们提出了一种体积自适应k空间采集框架，该框架联合学习在整个MRI体积中在哪里以及采样多少。我们的方法仅使用采集到的自动校准信号(ACS)测量，利用体积范围内的解剖信息，自适应地在切片间分配采样预算，同时识别信息丰富的k空间线。一个学习到的联合切片-频率细化模块协调采样决策，同时保持精确的总体积级采集预算。为了重建采集到的测量数据，我们设计了一个敏感度感知的同步交叉切片重建网络，该网络从ACS测量中估计线圈敏感度，并逐步细化相邻切片重建，同时强制执行硬k空间数据一致性。这两个网络都使用基于重建的监督进行联合优化，在推理时不需要完全采样的k空间。在多种对比度和加速因子下的膝盖和大脑MRI实验证明了我们采集框架的自适应行为，并评估了其重建性能。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一个体积自适应k空间采集框架，旨在解决传统加速MRI中预定义采样模式和统一预算的局限性。该框架利用ACS测量和体积范围内的解剖信息，智能地学习在哪里以及采样多少，以自适应地分配采样预算和识别关键k空间线。同时，引入一个敏感度感知的同步交叉切片重建网络进行图像重建，并与采集网络联合优化。实验结果表明，该方法在加速MRI方面表现出良好的自适应采样和重建性能。
AI.keywords: 加速MRI, k空间采集, 体积自适应, 深度学习, 图像重建
AI.comments: 这项工作通过引入体积自适应的k空间采集策略，显著提升了加速MRI的效率和灵活性。其创新点在于联合学习采样位置和数量，并结合敏感度感知的交叉切片重建，克服了传统方法对解剖变异的忽视。这种端到端的学习方法，特别是无需在推理时提供完全采样的k空间，具有重要的实际应用价值。

title: VESPA: Verifiable Symbolic Policy Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) aims to prevent agents from taking actions that are dangerous or destructive to their environment. This is especially important for safety-critical domains, such as robotics or autonomous driving. Formal verification can be used to prove agent safety through safety constraints. However, in practice, many policies do violate safety constraints, and thus are verified to be unsafe. Since the goal is to obtain a safe policy, we would need to retrain a new policy from scratch and then verify it again until a candidate happens to pass. Both training and verification are usually not cheap, which makes this process inefficient. We introduce VESPA ($\textbf{VE}$rifiable $\textbf{S}$ymbolic $\textbf{P}$olicy $\textbf{A}$daptation), a framework for targeted fine-tuning of decision tree policies. We show that using counterexamples for policy adaptation can make existing unsafe policies safe, or at least make considerable progress towards safety. Targeted fine-tuning of the existing policy on those counterexamples enables it to learn how to avoid violating safety constraints. We thus use the result of a formal verification as a training signal for fine-tuning. On CartPole, VESPA raises the mean number of verified safe steps from 63.8 to at least 92.7, reaching after two iterations what the same loop without counterexamples reaches after ten. On MountainCarContinuous, VESPA turns an unsafe policy into a safe policy in 53 of 60 runs. We conclude that counterexamples from a verifier are an effective training signal, which can be utilized to systematically improve the safety of policies. Our implementation is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/VESPA-Submission/

AI.title_translation: VESPA：面向安全强化学习的可验证符号策略自适应
AI.tldr: 论文提出VESPA框架，利用形式化验证的反例对决策树策略进行微调，从而高效地将不安全策略转化为安全策略。
AI.motivation: 传统的安全强化学习中，当策略被形式化验证证明为不安全时，往往需要从头重新训练并再次验证，这一过程成本高昂且效率低下。因此需要一种更高效的方法来修复现有的不安全策略。
AI.method: 提出VESPA框架，利用决策树策略的有针对性微调，将形式化验证产生的不安全反例作为训练信号，指导策略学习如何避免违反安全约束。
AI.result: 在CartPole任务中，VESPA将平均验证安全步数从63.8提升至至少92.7，仅需两轮迭代即可达到无反例循环十轮的效果；在MountainCarContinuous任务中，VESPA在60次运行中有53次成功将不安全策略转化为安全策略。
AI.conclusion: 形式化验证器提供的反例是一种有效的训练信号，可用于系统性地提升策略的安全性。
AI.translation: 安全强化学习（RL）旨在防止智能体采取对环境危险或具破坏性的行动，这对于机器人或自动驾驶等安全关键领域尤通过安全约束证明智能体的安全性。然而，在实践中，许多策略确实会违反安全约束，因此被验证为是不安全的。既然目标是获得一个安全的策略，我们需要从头重新训练一个新策略，然后再次验证，直到某个候选策略碰巧通过。训练和验证通常成本高昂，这使得整个过程效率低下。我们引入了VESPA（可验证符号策略自适应），这是一个用于决策树策略针对性微调的框架。我们证明了使用反例进行策略自适应可以使现有的不安全策略变得安全，或者至少在安全性方面取得实质性进展。针对这些反例对现有策略进行微调，使其能够学习如何避免违反安全约束。因此，我们利用形式化验证的结果作为微调的训练信号。在CartPole任务上，VESPA将平均验证安全步数从63.8提高到至少92.7，在两次迭代后达到了没有反例的循环需要十次迭代才能达到的效果。在MountainCarContinuous任务上，VESPA在60次运行中有53次将不安全策略转化为安全策略。我们得出结论，来自验证器的反例是一种有效的训练信号，可用于系统地提高策略的安全性。我们的实现可在以下网址获取：https://anonymous.4open.science/r/VESPA-Submission/
AI.summary: 论文提出了VESPA（可验证符号策略自适应）框架，通过将形式化验证中的反例作为训练信号来对决策树策略进行有针对性的微调，从而高效地将不安全策略转化为安全策略。
AI.keywords: 安全强化学习, 形式化验证, 策略自适应, 决策树, 反例微调
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将形式化验证中的反例作为训练信号，用于决策树策略的有针对性微调，从而高效地将不安全策略转化为安全策略，避免了从头训练的高昂成本。

title: From Restoration to Redrawing: Revitalizing Ancient Chinese Characters by SVG Code Generation and Editing
summary: Hanjian manuscripts written on Han Dynasty bamboo and wooden slips are invaluable heritage of ancient Chinese writing but suffer from damaged ink and incomplete strokes. Existing image-to-image restoration methods may alter observed strokes and offer limited control over stroke geometry. Inspired by experts' manual redrawing practices, we address these issues by introducing \textbf{ReDraw}, a two-stage vision-language model(VLM) that reformulates character restoration as Scalable Vector Graphics(SVG) code generation and editing. Stage one targets faithful vectorization of observed strokes geometry or conservative tracing of mildly degraded strokes. Guided by skeleton chain-of-thought reasoning and reinforcement learning with structure-aware rewards, stage two predicts skeletons before contours to redraw severely incomplete strokes by appending paths while keeping existing SVG paths unchanged. To support training, we develop a multi-layer data synthesis pipeline that disentangles ink, material, and degradation to generate 1.2M samples, and derive up to 6,400 adaptation pairs from 320 annotated real glyphs. Experiments demonstrate synthetic restoration performance and adaptability to real Hanjian glyphs. Code and demo will be available upon acceptance.

AI.title_translation: 从修复到重绘：通过SVG代码生成与编辑重焕古汉字生机
AI.tldr: 本文提出了ReDraw模型，通过将古汉字汉简的修复转化为SVG代码的生成与编辑，利用视觉语言模型和强化学习实现了对残损古汉字的精准矢量化与智能重绘。
AI.motivation: 汉朝竹木简上的汉简手稿是珍贵的古汉字遗产，但常常遭受墨迹损坏和笔画不完整的困扰。现有的图像到图像恢复方法可能会改变观察到的笔画，并且对笔画几何形状的控制有限。受专家手动重绘实践的启发，本文旨在解决这些问题。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为ReDraw的两阶段视觉语言模型（VLM），将字符修复转化为SVG代码生成和编辑。第一阶段针对观察到的笔画几何形状进行忠实的矢量化或对轻度退化笔画进行保守描摹；第二阶段在骨骼思维链推理和具有结构感知奖励的强化学习指导下，先预测骨骼再预测轮廓，通过追加路径来重绘严重残缺的笔画，同时保持现有SVG路径不变。此外，开发了一个多层数据合成流水线，生成1.2M样本，并从320个注释的真实字形中推导出多达6,400个适应对。
AI.result: 实验证明了该方法在合成恢复性能以及对真实汉简字体的适应性方面的有效性。
AI.conclusion: 论文成功开发了ReDraw模型和多层数据合成流水线，有效实现了汉简字符的忠实矢量化与严重残缺笔画的智能重绘，表现出优异的合成修复性能与对真实汉简字体的适应性。
AI.translation: 书写在汉代简牍上的汉简是珍贵的古汉字文化遗产，但往往面临墨迹受损和笔画残缺的问题。现有的图像到图像修复方法可能会改变观测到的笔画，且对笔画几何形状的控制有限。受专家人工重绘实践的启发，我们引入了ReDraw，这是一个两阶段的视觉语言模型（VLM），它将字符修复重新构想为可缩放矢量图形（SVG）代码的生成和编辑。第一阶段旨在对观测到的笔画几何形状进行忠实的矢量化，或对轻度退化的笔画进行保守描摹。在骨架思维链推理和具有结构感知奖励的强化学习指导下，第二阶段在预测轮廓之前先预测骨架，通过追加路径来重绘严重残缺的笔画，同时保持现有的SVG路径不变。为了支持训练，我们开发了一个多层数据合成流水线，将墨迹、材质和退化进行解耦以生成120万个样本，并从320个标注的真实字形中衍生出多达6400个适应对。实验证明了其合成修复性能以及对真实汉简字形的适应能力。代码和演示将在接收后提供。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了ReDraw，一个用于汉简字符修复的两阶段视觉语言模型。通过将字符恢复重新构想为SVG代码生成和编辑，该方法结合了骨骼思维链推理和结构感知强化学习，能够实现对受损古汉字的高效矢量化与严重残缺笔画的智能重绘。
AI.keywords: 汉简, 视觉语言模型, 可缩放矢量图形, 字符重绘, 强化学习
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的基于视觉语言模型和SVG代码生成的汉简字符修复与重绘方法（ReDraw），通过将图像修复转化为矢量图形的生成与编辑，克服了传统图像到图像方法的局限性，在古文字数字化保护领域具有重要的应用价值。

title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
summary: Evaluating distributed large language model (LLM) serving on heterogeneous edge devices requires exploring diverse model partitions, device placements, and network conditions, making repeated physical experiments costly. An efficient simulator for edge LLM serving must support diverse, fine-grained placement configurations, capture runtime behavior, and accurately predict execution times while keeping simulation overhead low. We present LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for fast, fine-grained evaluation of distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices without executing tensor operations. LEDGE constructs event graphs supporting non-uniform tensor and pipeline parallelism, estimates execution costs using reusable performance models calibrated from end-to-end measurements, and simulates shared-link contention. We evaluate LEDGE on a heterogeneous testbed of 10 Jetson and Raspberry Pi devices, covering 17 model--precision combinations across 4 LLM families. On Qwen deployments, LEDGE achieves request-level mean absolute percentage errors below 3.6% and a 135.3 times aggregate speedup over physical inference. Performance model calibrated on one LLM family yield 7.44% zero-shot end-to-end latency MAPE across three other families. Further simulations show how shared-link contention affects placement decisions and network topology constrains scaling. Across four edge environments, LEDGE completes 26,773 simulation runs in 83.8 minutes, enabling efficient exploration of deployment strategies under diverse resource conditions and serving objectives. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/gdfwj/LEDGE.

AI.title_translation: LEDGE：异构边缘设备上分布式大模型服务的高效模拟器
AI.tldr: LEDGE是一个轻量级、高效的模拟器，能够在无需实际运行张量运算的情况下，准确且快速地评估异构边缘设备上的分布式大模型服务。
AI.motivation: 在异构边缘设备上评估分布式大语言模型（LLM）服务需要探索各种模型分区、设备放置和网络条件，重复进行物理实验成本高昂，因此需要一个高效且准确的模拟器。
AI.method: 提出LEDGE模拟器，不执行实际张量运算，通过构建支持非均匀张量和流水线并行的事件图、使用从端到端测量中校准的可复用性能模型来估计执行成本，并模拟共享链路争用。
AI.result: 在10个异构边缘设备组成的测试台上评估显示，LEDGE在Qwen部署上的请求级平均绝对百分比误差（MAPE）低于3.6%，比物理推理快135.3倍；零样本端到端延迟的MAPE为7.44%，并在83.8分钟内完成了26,773次模拟运行。
AI.conclusion: LEDGE通过事件图建模和可复用的性能模型，实现了在异构边缘设备上高效、准确地模拟分布式大模型服务，极大降低了评估成本并加速了部署策略的探索。
AI.translation: 在异构边缘设备上评估分布式大语言模型（LLM）服务需要探索多样化的模型分区、设备放置和网络条件，这使得重复的物理实验成本高昂。一个高效的边缘LLM服务模拟器必须支持多样化、细粒度的放置配置，捕获运行时行为，并准确预测执行时间，同时保持较低的模拟开销。我们提出了LEDGE，这是一个轻量级的模拟器，用于在异构边缘设备上对分布式LLM服务进行快速、细粒度的评估，而无需执行张量运算。LEDGE构建了支持非均匀张量和流水线并行的事件图，使用从端到端测量中校准的可复用性能模型来估计执行成本，并模拟共享链路争用。我们在由10个Jetson和Raspberry Pi设备组成的异构测试台上评估了LEDGE，涵盖了4个LLM系列的17种模型-精度组合。在Qwen部署中，LEDGE实现了低于3.6%的请求级平均绝对百分比误差（MAPE），并且比物理推理获得了135.3倍的总体加速。在一个LLM系列上校准的性能模型在其他三个系列上产生了7.44%的零样本端到端延迟MAPE。进一步的模拟展示了共享链路争用如何影响放置决策以及网络拓扑如何限制扩展。在四个边缘环境中，LEDGE在83.8分钟内完成了26,773次模拟运行，从而能够在不同的资源条件和Serving目标下高效探索部署策略。源代码已在 https://github.com/gdfwj/LEDGE 公开。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了LEDGE，一个用于在异构边缘设备上进行分布式LLM服务快速、细粒度评估的轻量级模拟器。它通过事件图和性能校准模型，在无需实际执行张量运算的情况下，准确预测执行时间并模拟网络争用，从而高效探索不同的部署策略。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型服务, 边缘计算, 异构设备, 模拟器, 分布式推理
AI.comments: LEDGE是一个针对异构边缘设备上分布式大模型服务的创新高效模拟器。通过避免实际的张量运算和事件图建模，它在保持极高准确性的同时大幅降低了评估成本，对边缘AI部署策略的探索具有重要意义。

title: Constructing Dynamic Conversations with Neural Back-channel Generation and Voice-line Scheduling
summary: We present a novel approach to the problem of combining two voice-line channels of dyadic conversational audio into a unified conversation with controllable back-channeling and turn-taking dynamics. In voice performances for the game industry, the two tracks of voice-lines are typically recorded or synthesized in isolation. Our method takes two such unsynchronized tracks and uses a neural scheduler to sequence them into a single dynamic conversation, modifying both tracks by inserting or removing pauses and introducing voice overlap as appropriate. We further propose a back-channel predictor that is able to predict opportunity for back-channels for a given conversational turn's audio and content, which the scheduler can then incorporate. We evaluate our scheduler and predictor independently and in combination by: various quantitative comparison; a qualitative and perceptual comparison to prior art and naive baselines; a compelling set of results showing animator control over the diversity, extent and nature of back-channeling and turn dynamics.

AI.title_translation: 利用神经反馈生成和语音调度构建动态对话
AI.tldr: 提出了一种利用神经调度和反馈生成将独立录制的双人语音轨合成为自然、动态交互对话的新方法。
AI.motivation: 游戏行业中的双人对话音轨通常是独立录制或合成的，缺乏自然的反馈（back-channeling）和轮转（turn-taking）动态，因此需要一种方法将它们合成为一个具有可控动态的统一对话。
AI.method: 使用神经调度器对两个未同步的音轨进行排序和修改（插入/移除停顿、引入语音重叠），并提出反馈预测器来预测反馈机会并由调度器整合。
AI.result: 通过定量比较、定性与感知比较以及动画师控制实验，证明了该调度器和预测器在多样性、广度和反馈及轮转动态本质上的有效性。
AI.conclusion: 提出的神经调度器和反馈预测器能有效将独立语音轨融合成自然的、具交互性的动态对话。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一种新方法，用于将双人对话音频的两个语音通道组合成一个具有可控反馈和轮转动态的统一对话。在游戏行业的语音表演中，通常会独立录制或合成两个轨道的语音。我们的方法采用两个这样未同步的音轨，并使用神经调度器将它们排序为单一的动态对话，通过插入或移除停顿以及适当地引入语音重叠来修改这两个音轨。我们进一步提出了一种反馈预测器，能够根据给定对话回合的音频和内容预测反馈机会，调度器随后可以将其整合进来。我们通过各种定量比较、与先前技术及朴素基线的定性与感知比较，以及展示动画师对反馈和轮转动态的多样性、广度及本质的控制能力的一组引人注目的结果，对我们的调度器和预测器进行了独立和组合评估。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种将两个独立的语音音轨融合成统一动态对话的新方法。该方法利用神经调度器来调整停顿和重叠，并结合反馈预测器来预测并插入对话反馈，实现了对对话动态的可控管理。
AI.keywords: 对话生成, 神经调度器, 反馈生成, 轮转管理, 语音合成
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地提出结合神经反馈生成与语音调度来合成自然的动态对话，解决了游戏行业中独立录制音轨缺乏互动感的问题。然而，摘要中未提及具体的模型架构细节。

title: UCLIR: Unsupervised Continual Learning using Independent Representations
summary: In continual learning, regularization-based methods aim to mimic neuroplasticity by updating network weights to learn new tasks while constraining changes to parameters that are important for previously learned tasks through penalty terms. However, as the number of tasks increases, preserving knowledge from earlier tasks becomes less effective. This is mainly because updates for new tasks are distributed across the entire network, where parameters are highly interdependent due to the dense connectivity between neurons. Inspired by the Exponential Distance Rule (EDR), which states that the number of neural connections decreases with increasing physical distance, learning is naturally locally correlated while inter-area updates remain less task-dependent. Motivated by this principle, in this paper we demonstrate that applying weight regularization to multiple small and independently learned complementary representations is more effective than regularizing a single large shared representation. By decomposing the input into independently learned components, learning new tasks induces only localized parameter updates within specific representation, which limit interference and improve knowledge retention across tasks. We employ independent autoencoders that learn different parts of the input independently through unsupervised regularization. At inference time, a linear classifier is used for evaluation. The experimental results on a sequence of tasks using 5-Splits MNIST, sequence of 5-datasets, 5-Splits CIFAR-10, 10-Splits Tiny ImageNet shows competitive results with supervised and replay-based methods. Code is available.

AI.title_translation: UCLIR：使用独立表示的无监督持续学习
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为UCLIR的无监督持续学习方法，通过将输入分解为多个独立学习的表示来限制参数更新范围，从而有效克服灾难性遗忘。
AI.motivation: 传统的基于正则化的持续学习方法在任务增多时，由于参数高度互连，更新会分布在整个网络中，导致早期知识的保留效果变差。受生物学中指数距离规则（EDR）的启发，作者旨在探讨将权重正则化应用于多个小型、独立学习的互补表示是否比正则化单个大型共享表示更有效。
AI.method: 采用多个独立的自编码器，通过无监督正则化独立学习输入的不用部分，将大网络分解为多个独立学习的互补表示，并在推理时使用线性分类器进行评估。
AI.result: 在 5-Splits MNIST、5个数据集序列、5-Splits CIFAR-10 和 10-Splits Tiny ImageNet 等任务序列上的实验结果表明，该方法取得了与有监督和基于回放的方法相竞争的性能。
AI.conclusion: 基于独立表示的无监督持续学习方法（UCLIR）能够有效解决持续学习中的参数冲突与知识遗忘问题，在多个基准测试上取得了与有监督和基于回放方法相媲美的竞争性结果。
AI.translation: 在持续学习中，基于正则化的方法旨在模仿神经可塑性，通过惩罚项更新网络权重以学习新任务，同时约束对先前学习任务重要的参数的变化。然而，随着任务数量的增加，保留早期任务的知识变得越来越不有效。这主要是因为新任务的更新分布在整个网络中，由于神经元之间的密集连接，参数高度相互依赖。受指数距离规则（EDR）的启发——该规则指出神经连接的数量随着物理距离的增加而减少——学习自然是局部相关的，而区域间的更新对任务的依赖性较小。受这一原则的启发，在本文中，我们证明了将权重正则化应用于多个小型且独立学习的互补表示，比正则化单个大型共享表示更有效。通过将输入分解为独立学习的组件，学习新任务只会引起特定表示内局部的参数更新，从而限制干扰并改善跨任务的知识保留。我们采用独立的自编码器，通过无监督正则化独立学习输入的不同部分。在推理时，使用线性 classifier 进行评估。在包含5-Splits MNIST、5个数据集序列、5-Splits CIFAR-10和10-Splits Tiny ImageNet的任务序列上的实验结果显示，该方法取得了与有监督和基于回放的方法相媲美的竞争性结果。代码已开源。
AI.summary: 论文提出了UCLIR方法，这是一种基于独立表示的无监督持续学习框架。它利用独立的自编码器学习互补的输入表示，将参数更新局限于特定的表示中，从而减少任务间干扰并提高知识保留能力。
AI.keywords: 持续学习, 无监督学习, 独立表示, 指数距离规则, 灾难性遗忘
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将生物学中的指数距离规则（EDR）应用于无监督持续学习中，通过将输入分解为多个独立学习的表示来替代传统的单一共享表示，有效缓解了灾难性遗忘，且不依赖回放数据或监督信号。

title: Object Pose: The Link between Weak Perspective, Paraperspective, and Full Perspective
summary: Recently, DeMenthon and Davis [4,5] proposed a method for determining the pose of a 3-D object with respect to a camera from 3-D to 2-D point correspondences. The method consists of iteratively improving the pose computed with a weak perspective camera model to converge, at the limit, to a pose estimation computed with a perspective camera model. In this paper we give an algebraic derivation of DeMenthon and Davis' method and we show that it belongs to a larger class of methods where the perspective camera model is approximated either at zero order (weak perspective) or first order (paraperspective). We describe in detail an iterative paraperspective pose computation method for both non coplanar and coplanar object points. We analyse the convergence of these methods and we conclude that the iterative paraperspective method (proposed in this paper) has better convergence properties than the iterative weak perspective method. We introduce a simple way of taking into account the orthogonality constraint associated with the rotation matrix. We analyse the sensitivity to camera calibration errors and we define the optimal experimental setup with respect to imprecise camera calibration. We compare the results obtained with this method and with a non-linear optimization method.

AI.title_translation: 物体姿态：弱透视、准透视和全透视之间的联系
AI.tldr: 本文对DeMenthon和Davis的迭代弱透视姿态估计方法进行了代数推导，并将其归类到一个更大的方法族中，该族通过零阶或一阶近似透视相机模型。文章详细介绍了一种迭代准透视姿态计算方法，并证明其收敛性优于迭代弱透视方法，并探讨了相机标定误差的敏感性。
AI.motivation: DeMenthon和Davis最近提出了一种从3D到2D点对应关系确定3D物体相对于相机的姿态的方法，该方法通过迭代改进弱透视模型计算的姿态来收敛到透视相机模型。本文的动机是对该方法进行代数推导，并将其置于一个更广阔的背景下，即透视相机模型可以通过零阶（弱透视）或一阶（准透视）近似。
AI.method: 本文对DeMenthon和Davis的方法进行了代数推导，并展示了它属于一个更大的方法类别，该类别通过零阶（弱透视）或一阶（准透视）近似透视相机模型。文章详细描述了一种针对非共面和共面物体点的迭代准透视姿态计算方法。作者分析了这些方法的收敛性，并引入了一种考虑旋转矩阵正交性约束的简单方法。此外，还分析了对相机标定误差的敏感性，并定义了针对不精确相机标定的最佳实验设置，并与非线性优化方法进行了结果比较。
AI.result: 研究结果表明，本文提出的迭代准透视方法比迭代弱透视方法具有更好的收敛性。此外，还引入了一种考虑旋转矩阵正交性约束的简单方法，并分析了相机标定误差的敏感性，定义了针对不精确相机标定的最佳实验设置。
AI.conclusion: 迭代准透视方法（本文提出）比迭代弱透视方法具有更好的收敛性。
AI.translation: 最近，DeMenthon和Davis [4,5] 提出了一种从3D到2D点对应关系确定3D物体相对于相机的姿态的方法。该方法包括迭代改进用弱透视相机模型计算的姿态，使其最终收敛到用透视相机模型计算的姿态估计。在本文中，我们对DeMenthon和Davis的方法进行了代数推导，并表明它属于一类更大的方法，其中透视相机模型通过零阶（弱透视）或一阶（准透视）近似。我们详细描述了一种针对非共面和共面物体点的迭代准透视姿态计算方法。我们分析了这些方法的收敛性，并得出结论，迭代准透视方法（本文提出）比迭代弱透视方法具有更好的收敛性。我们介绍了一种考虑与旋转矩阵相关的正交性约束的简单方法。我们分析了对相机标定误差的敏感性，并定义了针对不精确相机标定的最佳实验设置。我们将用此方法和非线性优化方法获得的结果进行了比较。
AI.summary: 本文对DeMenthon和Davis提出的迭代弱透视姿态估计方法进行了代数推导，并将其归类到通过零阶（弱透视）或一阶（准透视）近似透视相机模型的更大方法族中。文章详细介绍了一种迭代准透视姿态计算方法，并分析了其收敛性，发现其优于迭代弱透视方法。此外，文中还提出了一种处理旋转矩阵正交性约束的简单方法，并分析了相机标定误差的敏感性，定义了最佳实验设置，并与非线性优化方法进行了比较。
AI.keywords: 物体姿态, 弱透视, 准透视, 透视模型, 姿态估计
AI.comments: 本文通过对现有姿态估计算法进行代数推导和归类，提供了一个更广阔的理论框架。其创新点在于提出了迭代准透视方法，并证明了其在收敛性上的优越性。此外，对正交性约束的处理和对相机标定误差的敏感性分析，也增加了方法的实用性和鲁棒性。这对于计算机视觉领域，特别是物体姿态估计的研究具有重要意义。

title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
comments: Accepted to KDD 2027. Project page is at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page
summary: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. To address the evaluation gap, we introduce RoughCut-Bench, which covers two practical settings: (1) a visually driven setting over video cases, covering highlight detection and selection, source-video ordering, and adherence to user requirements when provided; and (2) a speech-driven setting over automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts, covering filler removal, expression deduplication, and low-value content trimming. Across these settings, the benchmark contains 101 visually driven cases, including 831 raw videos with 1,476 highlight annotations. It also includes 84 speech-driven cases, each consisting of an ASR transcript with annotated cleanup spans. The evaluation compares cut plans with these annotations in both settings and additionally uses a human-aligned agentic evaluator to assess rendered-cut quality in the visual setting. To apply LVLMs to automatic rough-cut, we further propose agentic workflows that guide them to produce structured cut plans from input materials. Experiments show that current LVLMs remain limited in producing expert-aligned cut plans. Our benchmark, code, and prompts are released at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page.
comment: Accepted to KDD 2027. Project page is at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page

AI.title_translation: 粗剪基准：用于大型视觉语言模型自动视频粗剪的基准
AI.tldr: 该研究提出了RoughCut-Bench，一个用于评估大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在视频粗剪任务中的表现的基准。该基准包含视觉驱动和语音驱动两类场景，并评估了LVLMs在生成结构化剪辑方案方面的能力，结果表明现有LVLMs仍有局限性。
AI.motivation: 自动视频粗剪在媒体制作中至关重要，但现有的大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在该领域的应用和评估仍显不足，缺乏全面的基准和成熟的工作流程。
AI.method: 提出了RoughCut-Bench基准，包含视觉驱动（高亮检测与选择、源视频排序、满足用户需求）和语音驱动（去除填充词、去重、删减低价值内容）两类场景。基准包含101个视觉驱动案例（831个视频，1476个高亮标注）和84个语音驱动案例（含ASR文本和标注的清理片段）。还提出了引导LVLMs生成结构化剪辑方案的代理工作流程，并使用人类对齐的代理评估器评估视觉场景下的剪辑质量。
AI.result: 实验表明，当前的大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在生成符合专家水平的剪辑方案方面能力有限。
AI.conclusion: RoughCut-Bench为评估和推动视频粗剪任务中的LVLMs研究提供了重要的资源。尽管现有模型存在局限性，但该基准为未来的研究和开发奠定了基础。
AI.translation: 视频粗剪是媒体制作工作流程中的核心阶段，将原始媒体素材组织成初始视频剪辑。尽管大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在视频相关任务方面取得了最新进展，但自动粗剪仍未得到充分探索，缺乏用于评估的全面基准或用于生成可执行剪辑方案的成熟工作流程。为解决评估差距，我们引入了RoughCut-Bench，它涵盖了两个实际场景：（1）基于视频案例的视觉驱动场景，包括高亮检测和选择、源视频排序以及在提供用户需求时满足这些需求；（2）基于自动语音识别（ASR）转录的语音驱动场景，包括填充词去除、表达去重和低价值内容修剪。在该基准中，包含101个视觉驱动案例，涉及831个原始视频和1,476个高亮标注。它还包括84个语音驱动案例，每个案例由一个带有标注清理片段的ASR转录组成。评估在两个场景下将剪辑方案与这些标注进行比较，并在视觉场景中额外使用一个人类对齐的代理评估器来评估渲染剪辑的质量。为了将LVLMs应用于自动粗剪，我们进一步提出了代理工作流程，引导它们从输入材料中生成结构化剪辑方案。实验表明，当前的LVLMs在生成符合专家水平的剪辑方案方面仍然有限。我们的基准、代码和提示可在https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page 获取。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了RoughCut-Bench，一个全面的基准，用于评估大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在视频粗剪任务中的表现。该基准涵盖了视觉驱动和语音驱动两种场景，并包含了大量的视频和文本数据。研究还提出了新的代理工作流程来指导LVLMs生成剪辑方案，并通过实验发现当前LVLMs在这一任务上仍存在局限性。
AI.keywords: 视频粗剪, 视觉语言模型, 基准测试, 代理工作流程, 媒体制作
AI.comments: 该研究在视频粗剪这一重要但研究不足的领域做出了贡献，提出了一个全面的基准（RoughCut-Bench）以及相应的评估方法和代理工作流程。基准的设计考虑了实际应用场景，并包含了丰富的标注数据。然而，研究结果表明当前LVLMs在该任务上的表现仍有待提高，这为未来的研究指明了方向。该基准的发布将有助于推动该领域的发展。

title: A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange
summary: Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.

title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
summary: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. We evaluate TARS on four commercial robots across 44 experimental settings, conducting 133,400 executions. TARS uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment and achieves up to 94% verified action coverage.

title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents
summary: Organizations increasingly deploy downloaded open-weight GUI agents. A backdoored agent passes acceptance tests on clean data and misbehaves only when a visual trigger appears on screen, turning an unvetted checkpoint into a supply-chain risk. However, existing sample-level detectors target image classifiers and CLIP-style encoders, leaving step-level backdoor detection for GUI agents unaddressed. On clean steps, the instruction drives the action; when an unreferenced screen region hijacks the step, the instruction loses control over the decision state or that region dictates it instead. We term this signature intent--evidence dominance inversion and propose IDEA (Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit) to detect backdoor activation at inference time for each step without trigger knowledge or attack data. Specifically, Intent Counterfactual Probing (ICP) measures how far redirected instructions move the decision state, and Region Causal Audit (RCA) quantifies how far ablating a candidate region moves it. A gated conformal score compares both displacements against clean steps at the same distance from the clean manifold, providing a finite-sample false-positive guarantee. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B across five attack families show that IDEA consistently detects backdoor activation under a controlled false-positive rate and outperforms state-of-the-art detection methods, while localizing the trigger region for every alarm and adding only modest inference overhead.

title: SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement
summary: Predicting the RNA and protein content of cells from routine H&E images could extend spatial molecular profiling to existing slide archives. However, both H&E-spatial proteomics and H&E-spatial transcriptomics paired datasets are limited by the number of available markers and the insufficient availability of high-quality, cell-resolved data. We present SCOPE (Single-Cell Omics Prediction via RNA-protein prior Enhancement), a unified framework that leverages biologically complementary information between RNA and proteins to address the limited availability of single-omics supervision. Our key insight is that, although RNA and proteins represent distinct molecular modalities, their biological relationships provide valuable shared knowledge that can benefit single-omics prediction tasks. To this end, SCOPE introduces biologically informed biomarker priors to enhance shared gene-level representations, enabling knowledge transfer across RNA and protein modalities through gene-protein correspondence and molecular associations. By exploiting these complementary relationships, SCOPE enables both prediction tasks to benefit from a shared backbone enriched with cross-omics biological knowledge. Furthermore, its biomarker correlation design facilitates the prediction of unseen markers, extending spatially resolved molecular profiling beyond directly supervised targets. Across test datasets spanning 16 organs, SCOPE improves the average RNA Pearson correlation over the strongest baseline by 8.8%. On two external protein cohorts, it improves the average Pearson correlation over the strongest baseline by 9.7% for seen markers and 11.9% for unseen markers.

title: Laguerre-MPPI
summary: Model Predictive Path Integral control (MPPI) is a sampling-based control method that handles nonlinear dynamics and non-convex costs without gradient information. Since MPPI samples the entire input sequence, longer prediction horizons lead to a higher-dimensional sampling space, potentially degrading control performance. This paper proposes Laguerre-MPPI, which parameterizes the control input sequence using discrete-time Laguerre basis functions and samples the basis coefficients. The resulting search dimension is independent of the prediction horizon. Hence, a longer prediction horizon does not require more samples to maintain the sampling density. For linear systems with quadratic costs, we derive a closed-loop stability condition in the infinite-sample limit. Under finite sampling, we provide a closed-form expression for the limit of the ratio of the effective sample size to the number of samples. We also show that the upper bound of this limit for Laguerre-MPPI is no lower than that for conventional MPPI. Numerical experiments demonstrate smoother inputs in obstacle avoidance and maintained performance over long horizons. Moreover, they verify the lower bound on the number of samples given by the finite-sample analysis.

title: Asymmetric Decomposition for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Unassigned Agents
summary: Robots without assigned tasks may obstruct active robots, while routing them to designated parking locations can cause unnecessary travel. This article proposes flow-oracle conflict-based search (FOCBS) for Multi-Agent Path Finding with unassigned agents (MAPF-UA). FOCBS searches over assigned-agent paths using conflict-based search (CBS) and routes targetless unassigned agents through a min-cost flow oracle. When the selected assigned-agent paths leave unassigned agents no collision-free paths, flow-conflict branching converts min-cut blockers into assigned-agent constraints, which guide the search without excluding optimal solutions. A batched zero-cost warm start accelerates the oracle, and start-avoiding tie-breaking reduces unassigned-agent movement. For feasible instances on finite graphs, we prove termination and global minimization of assigned-agent sum of service time, measured by last-arrival times. Unassigned-agent movement is minimized conditional on the selected assigned-agent paths, without a global lexicographic optimality guarantee. Benchmark experiments show that FOCBS scales well with the number of unassigned agents, and ablation studies show that, compared with discarding non-completable assigned-agent paths, flow-conflict branching solves substantially more instances while retaining optimality. Simulation and physical-robot experiments demonstrate plan executability, with laboratory tests reducing fleet travel by 40.8% relative to the parking-based coordination baseline. The source code and related resources are available at https://github.com/Chin-hsi/focbs

title: PIVOT: Distribution-Preserving Multi-BitWatermarking with Minimax-Optimal Scoring
summary: As LLM-generated content becomes increasingly widespread, reliable attribution calls for multi-bit watermarks that embed recoverable messages without distorting the output distribution. We introduce PIVOT, a multi-bit watermark with model-free verification based on mirrored rank-interval sampling. At each generation step, PIVOT uses a keyed pseudorandom scalar and a secret permutation of the vocabulary. The message bit determines whether next-token probability intervals are arranged in forward or reverse secret-rank order. Sampling from these mirrored layouts preserves every token probability exactly while inducing an opposite-signed dependence between the scalar and the sampled token's secret rank. This dependence yields a pivotal rank statistic whose null distribution is invariant to the unknown next-token law, enabling model-free calibration and decoding. We formulate joint watermark detection and message recovery as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem, derive a moment-robust minimax-optimal detection score over a relaxed moment class, and establish finite-sample recovery guarantees. Extensive experiments on two representative large language models validate the effectiveness of PIVOT, demonstrating reliable watermark detection and message recovery while preserving the generator's output distribution.

title: The 7th International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026): Summary and Results
summary: This report summarizes the seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Com- petition (VNN-COMP 2026), held as part of the Symposium on AI Verification (SAIV) co-located with the International Conference on Computer-Aided Verification (CAV) at FLoC 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. The goal of the competition is to provide an objective comparison of the state-of-the-art methods in neural network verification, in terms of scal- ability and speed. Along this line, we used standard formats (ONNX for neural networks and VNNLIB for specifications), standard hardware (all tools are run by the organizers on AWS), and tool parameters provided by the tool authors. This report summarizes the rules, benchmarks, participating tools, results, and lessons learned from this competition.

title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: Long-horizon tasks in embodied and web environments involve extended decision sequences and delayed feedback, making accurate planning crucial for success. World models tackle this by learning latent dynamics for imagination-based planning. However, existing approaches merely rely on dense pixel-level observations, which forces the model to absorb redundant information while overlooking relations among task-relevant entities. Consequently, small errors may accumulate over long imagined rollouts and gradually corrupt the predictions. In this paper, we explore world models that imagine over sparse state abstractions, which poses two key challenges: 1) how to remove redundant information and form a compact state abstraction; 2) how to incorporate the relational structure to learn reliable long-horizon dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose Embodied Graph, a relational state abstraction that supports structured dynamics modeling and long-horizon imagination, and the Relational World Model (RWM), which performs imagination directly over graph states. RWM consists of (i) a Task-Aware Embodied Graph Constructor that filters redundant details and maintains graph memory through online updates, and (ii) an Embodied Graph Recurrent State Space Model that learns node-wise latent dynamics while capturing inter-node dependencies. The imagined graph states provide predictions of action consequences to guide decision-making. Experiments on Minecraft and Crafter demonstrate the effectiveness of RWM in embodied environments. Notably, in Minecraft, RWM is the only method that obtains diamonds within the given budget. Experiments on web interaction further illustrate the applicability of relational state prediction to the decision making process of web agents.

title: EVF-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for E-commerce Visual Effects in Video Generation
summary: E-commerce visual effects (EVF) are dynamic, product-centered visual presentations in e-commerce videos, often accompanied by promotional text. They play an important role in attracting viewer attention and conveying product information. However, general measures of visual quality and text relevance alone do not establish whether generated videos preserve product appearance, maintain readable text, and produce coherent, contextually appropriate effects. To address this issue, we introduce EVF-Bench, a dedicated benchmark spanning six evaluation dimensions: visual quality and text relevance as general dimensions, and motion, product consistency, text stability, and creative rationality as EVF-specific dimensions. To complement the benchmark and support task-aligned research and model adaptation, we further construct EVF-32K, a dataset of over 32000 curated image-text-video triples tailored to e-commerce scenarios. Using this suite, we systematically evaluate representative video generation models and their domain-adapted variants. The results reveal complementary strengths, with no evaluated configuration leading all six dimensions. Together, EVF-Bench and EVF-32K provide a task-oriented evaluation framework and a supporting data resource for e-commerce video generation.

title: eFAIR: Fair LLM Serving under Hourly Electricity Commitments
summary: Datacenters can procure electricity in day-ahead markets by committing to energy purchases for individual hours. For LLM services operating within these hourly budgets, maximizing aggregate throughput alone may still leave individual requests waiting or receiving much slower service than desired. Fair serving therefore requires improving service for poorly served requests while reserving electricity for later arrivals whose timing and demand are unknown. To compare service across requests, we define normalized throughput as each request's actual output rate divided by the product of its standalone throughput and its service entitlement, a positive weight representing its desired service level. Using this measure, we formulate fair serving as leximin optimization under an hourly electricity constraint, prioritizing requests with the lowest normalized throughput. To address this problem, we present eFAIR, an online scheduler that coordinates request dispatching, electricity budget allocation, and GPU frequency selection through a common normalized-throughput target. Specifically, request dispatching prioritizes requests by desired service level and progress; electricity budget allocation reserves electricity for current and expected future work; and frequency selection uses electricity savings to raise GPU frequencies for requests with higher desired service levels. Evaluations on H20 and H200 configurations, each with 32 replicas, show that eFAIR improves the tenth percentile of normalized throughput by 28.0%-31.0% over the best budget-feasible baseline, while keeping absolute deviations from the hourly electricity commitment below 0.26%. eFAIR also improves throughput balance among concurrent requests and aligns electricity allocation more closely with service demand over time. Together, these results demonstrate how eFAIR improves request-level fairness within an hourly commitment.

title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
summary: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. This retrospective study evaluated two generalist models, RADAR and Merlin, for differentiating liver tumors using a public single-institution multiphase CT dataset (517 cases: hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, breast and colorectal cancer liver metastases, and hemangioma). The models were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using their existing outputs and with linear probing, in which only a linear classifier was trained on frozen image features (stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated five times). In the zero-shot setting, RADAR achieved an accuracy of 54.4% (95% CI: 49.9, 58.8) and a $κ$ of 0.37 for four-class differentiation at the portal venous phase and predicted 31% (129 of 421) of malignant tumors as hemangioma. With linear probing of four-phase features, its accuracy improved to 79.9% (95% CI: 76.6, 83.4) with a $κ$ of 0.72, and 1% (five of 421) of malignant tumors were predicted as hemangioma; Merlin achieved an accuracy of 60.9% (95% CI: 56.9, 65.0). Generalist CT foundation models showed limited zero-shot ability to differentiate liver tumors, which improved substantially with linear probing alone.

title: QuantAtlas-OM: Taming Neural Spectral Bias in Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Ocean Dynamics
summary: Autoregressive neural networks exhibit spectral bias in long-horizon spatiotemporal prediction. As rollouts progress, high-frequency details decay, blurring the predicted fields and destabilizing long-range forecasts. Ocean dynamics offer a particularly stringent test because kinetic energy is concentrated in mesoscale eddies and fronts spanning tens of kilometers. This degradation stems from coupling large-scale phase evolution and small-scale energy retention in a shared feature space. Evolution on a coarse grid smooths out high-wavenumber eddies, whereas evolution on a fine grid amplifies small-scale phase errors and triggers rollout instability. We introduce QuantAtlas-OM (QuantAtlas Ocean Model), a scale-spectral decoupling framework that confines deep temporal evolution to a low-wavenumber latent manifold for long-term stability while routing full-resolution eddy and front residuals through an outer bypass to the decoder. Across physical regimes, the evolution core pairs non-local attention with resolution-invariant dilated spatial gating. Across three western boundary currents, QuantAtlas-OM retains $43.7\%$ to $86.5\%$ of mesoscale spectral energy along the $k^{-3}$ cascade at Day $120$, sustains anomaly correlation coefficients of $0.81$ to $0.88$ at Day $60$, and reaches $0.66$ at Day $120$ in the Kuroshio ($2.5\times$ to $7.7\times$ the best baselines). Trained at $0.25^\circ$, QuantAtlas-OM transfers zero-shot to a global $0.125^\circ$ grid ($0.81$ Day-$10$ spatial correlation) and leads global $0.25^\circ$, $23$-level 3D ocean simulations ($120$ days) and coupled ocean-atmosphere forecasts ($60$ days), ranking first on $15$ of $16$ metrics and cutting $60$- to $120$-day salinity RMSE by $13\%$ to $27\%$ across global ocean basins.

title: A Godunov-type in-cell discontinuous reconstruction shock-capturing method for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
summary: The present paper is devoted to show the correct convergence of a numerical method based on Godunov and the in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic but never recasts in a conservation form. With ambiguous nonconservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. In a previous work the authors determine the simple waves of the nonconservative system studied here and they are able to construct the solutions of the Riemann problem of interest. These solutions are used to obtain a Godunov-type scheme and it is combined with an in-cell discontinuous reconstruction technique to obtain the correct convergence to the exact solution even in the presence of shocks.

title: Evaluating LIM Trading Agents: A Critical Review of Backtesting Validity and Reporting Practices
comments: 8 pages, 1 figure, accepted by IEEE SSCI
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in investment research, and many studies report promising historical returns. However, such results are only credible if researchers can demonstrate that the model used only information available at the time, account for how strategies and configurations were selected, and explain how reported returns were generated. We identify six common threats to validity in LLM investment evaluations and apply them to 18 published studies. Across 108 assessments, we find substantial gaps in reporting. No paper fully addresses information timing, model-memory exposure, universe selection, trading costs, or configuration-selection bias. Only four studies provide minimum evidence that results hold across multiple market periods. Our analysis reveals that commonly used safeguards often address different problems than researchers assume. For example, using dated inputs does not guarantee that a pretrained model lacked knowledge of future events, and repeated experimental runs do not correct for strategy-selection bias. We therefore propose an evaluation protocol for future LLM investment research. Rather than judging whether LLMs can generate profits, our study examines whether existing evidence is sufficient to support such claims. We conclude that current reporting practices are generally insufficient for that purpose.

title: PULSAR-V: I/O-Aware Post-Update Attestation for RISC-V
summary: Post-update attestation proves that a device installed the intended firmware, not that the image stayed protected until the report was signed. In a multi-master SoC, a master outside the attested processor can corrupt update-critical memory. In contrast, the firmware identity, lifecycle state, and the CPU's protection evidence remain byte-identical to a healthy device's. We present PULSAR-V, a post-update attestation architecture which binds the authenticated update commit to the effective permissions and immutability of both gates (PMP/EPMP on the CPU, the I/O policy mediating DMA), sampled at the commit and at attestation, the I/O gate latching its own commit-time state in hardware. In a RISC-V SoC prototyped on a ZCU102 FPGA (CV32E40S core with 16 PMP regions, IOPMP-style unit, AXI write guard), a 256-byte write from the board's Arm DMA engine bypasses PMP and corrupts the committed image: every conventional claim stays true, and PULSAR-V rejects the device on its I/O-policy evidence alone. It also rejects an intact device whose policy left the image writable, a verdict no integrity check can reach. The gate and its commit latch cost 436 LUTs, 4.6% of the SoC, and evidence collection takes 43.1k cycles independent of image size, 41x less than re-hashing 16 KiB.

title: PatchAdaNet: Unsupervised class incremental learning using local patches and global adapters
summary: Biological learning systems acquire knowledge incrementally through broad, reusable representations established early and kept largely stable, while integrating new experience with minimal interference with previously learned knowledge. Replay-based methods approximate this by storing samples or features from previous tasks and mixing them into the current task. However, memory buffers grow with the number of tasks and may retain task-specific noise that reduces generalization. To address these limitations, we propose PatchAdaNet (Patch Adapter Network), an unsupervised class-incremental learning method for image classification that continually updates feature representations using autoencoders. Since images share structural features such as edges, corners, and shapes, we first divide each image into patches and train independent autoencoders on external data to reconstruct each patch. The layers of all patch encoders are aggregated into global frozen layers that generalize across tasks and remain fixed throughout learning. Learnable adapters then build global image representations from these features to reconstruct the entire image. To prevent feature drift without storing data, we introduce the Global Feature Centroid (GFC), a fixed-size running average of adapter outputs updated after each task to penalizes representation drift. Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) is applied to the learnable layers to preserve previously learned features by constraining important weights. Finally, a linear classifier is trained on the frozen latent representation and GFC for class-incremental evaluation. We evaluate PatchAdaNet in both CNN and Vision Transformer settings on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, miniImageNet and 5-Datasets, providing a comparative study of the two architectures under identical class-incremental settings. Code is available.

title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
summary: Embodied models depend on real interaction data, yet collecting it on physical robots is slow and labor-intensive. Recent ego-to-robot pipelines retarget first-person view human videos to robot data via transferring hand and arm motion. They judge fidelity mainly by visual appearance. However, trajectories often fail in terms of physics: fingers hover beside objects, and grippers close on empty space. We argue that how the object moves and the contacts that drive the motion count. Thus, we present Ego2X, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Ego2X centers on CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), which records each contact on the object by its surface anchor, as well as relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state. Throughout the pipeline, CORE corrects hand-object drift via object-relative constraints, steers inverse kinematics toward contacts the robot must realize, and preserves held objects during arm erasure and robot compositing. On HOT3D, contact-driven correction reduces in-contact hand depth error by 33.7%, while on EgoDex, contact-driven retargeting realizes 62.9% of annotated contacts, surpassing the official HuRo pipeline (27.9%). In RoboTwin 2.0, post-training X-VLA on Ego2X episodes alone, without simulator demonstrations, raises task success rate from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0% across 200 paired scenes. We will publicly release our conversion pipeline and CORE-annotated dataset for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.

title: BiPathCPG: A Novel Load-Sharing Design Architecture for Compound Planetary Gearboxes
comments: 8 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Project page: https://deepak-kapa.github.io/PancakeActuator/ Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
summary: Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) actuators are widely used in legged robots due to their low reflected inertia, high backdrivability, and high torque density, commonly employing planetary or cycloidal gearboxes. Single-stage planetary gearboxes offer high efficiency but limited torque density; multi-stage designs improve torque density at the cost of efficiency; and cycloidal gearboxes provide high stiffness but suffer from torque ripple. Compound Planetary Gearboxes (CPG) offer a compromise, but conventional designs result in increased actuator width, mass, and reduced torsional stiffness in 3D-printed actuators. This paper proposes the BiPath Compound Planetary Gearbox (BiPathCPG), a novel architecture that introduces an idle second-stage sun gear and load-sharing second-stage planets within the otherwise unused space of a conventional CPG to simultaneously improve stiffness, reduce actuator width, and reduce mass. An optimization framework computes BiPathCPG parameters for a given motor and target gear ratio. The architecture is validated through a 3D-printed proof-of-concept actuator design, benchmarked against a conventional CPG using custom-built test rigs. The BiPathCPG achieves a torsional stiffness of 1394 Nm/rad, a 1.70x improvement over the conventional CPG, with a 32% reduction in backlash, 25 g lower mass, and approximately 6.4 mm reduction in axial width, while achieving a peak stall torque of 36.49 Nm.

title: Inherited Adapter Experts for Replay-Free Domain-Incremental Learning
comments: 21 pages (8 pages main text, plus references and supplementary material), 8 figures, 23 tables
summary: Replay-free domain-incremental learning trains a model on the same classes in successive domains without keeping earlier images. Per-domain learners freeze a pre-trained ViT and train an additional expert for each new domain: the small set of parameters and the classification head learned on that domain. Test images carry no domain label, so a router selects one expert for each image. Recent work trains this router. However, a training-free Mahalanobis router costs the analyzed learners under 2.7 points of final accuracy relative to always selecting each image's own-domain expert. The experts, not this router, limit accuracy. Our learner, Lamarck, therefore uses this router and strengthens the experts. Its adapters, small trainable layers that correct every image token after each deep ViT block, add 4.4 points of final accuracy on the deepfake benchmark CDDB-Hard. In addition, each expert is initialized from its predecessor at no extra cost: the domains share their classes, so an image misrouted to a later expert loses less. Against twelve frozen-backbone baselines under one protocol, Lamarck is first on CDDB-Hard by 5.2 points, second on DomainNet and OfficeHome, and highest in mean accuracy.

title: Assessing Vision-Language Models for Early Prediction of Unsafe Situations in Robotics
comments: Submitted to ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process visual information and textual instructions and, by using their ability to understand and reason about context, are well-suited for predicting robot failures before they occur. However, evidence supporting this remains limited. To address this, we present an empirical evaluation of VLMs for predicting robot failures. In particular, we experiment with Qwen, InternVL, and LLaVA-OneVision across three robotic case studies (HuRoN, Pal Robotics, and CrowdBot), analyzing both video and odometry data for early failure warning (i.e., before an unsafe situation occurs). Specifically, we evaluate their performance in classifying situations as safe, potentially unsafe, and unsafe, together with uncertainty quantified using various metrics, and study the relationship between uncertainty and performance. Our results showed that Qwen provides the strongest overall classification and prediction-reliability performance, while InternVL shows stronger early-warning capability in several configurations. The results further show that the effect of robot-state information and temporal history depends on the model and evaluation objective. Overall, our findings indicate that general-purpose VLMs can support early robot-safety monitoring, but the most suitable configuration depends on whether the priority is accurate assessment of safety-state, reliable confidence and uncertainty, or timely warning before unsafe events.

title: Human-LLM Cognitive Extension: A Framework for Studying Coupled Cognition
summary: Recent research on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) reports divergent cognitive outcomes, including improved assisted performance, limited transfer, and compromised unaided learning. Here, we argue that part of this seeming inconsistency arises because studies often assess different cognitive systems without making the unit of analysis explicit. Building on work in extended and distributed cognition, we propose the Human-LLM Cognitive Extension (HLCE) as a methodological framework for matching experimental designs, measures, and causal inferences to four distinct systems: the human acting independently, the artificial agent, the joined human-LLM configuration, and the human after division. The framework also treats the coupling architecture as part of the experimental object. HLCE separates performance augmentation, system-level complementarity, post-interaction human change, and stronger claims of constitutive cognitive integration. This separation can improve the interpretation of existing evidence and guide the design of human-LLM interactions without assuming in advance that these configurations constitute extended minds. We illustrate the application of HLCE with a synthetic diagnostic experiment comparing two connecting configurations that differ in how supporting information is communicated. The example highlights how distinct couplings can shape the organization of joint problem-solving, even when the final outcome remains unchanged. Overall, HLCE provides a methodological basis for designing controlled experiments and interpreting evidence across distinct forms of human-LLM cognitive interaction.

title: SEER: Semantic Evidence for Executable Region Propagation in Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
summary: Training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) has made strong progress by adapting CLIP-like representations to dense prediction, but its remaining errors are often local, structured, and tied to the active label space. A successful correction must be visually plausible, legal under the target vocabulary, and executable in the segmentation score field. We propose SEER, a training-free test-time repair layer for Semantic Evidence and Executable Region propagation. SEER casts post-prediction OVSS repair as evidence-conditioned label propagation. The OVSS score space proposes compact candidate labels, a frozen VLM verifies closed-set regional evidence, and an execution gate certifies whether the evidence is legally and semantically actionable. The accepted label is then propagated by an OVSS-side policy: coherent high-confidence regions allow broad propagation, while object- or boundary-risk cases use conservative score-grounded propagation. Across eight standard OVSS benchmarks, SEER reaches 58.0 average mIoU without updating OVSS weights. Matched-input controls isolate the repair mechanism, while resource measurements report the cost of the complete frozen system.

title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
summary: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. To address these gaps, we introduce Game2Player, a framework that co-develops game environments and players to collect diverse and verifiable gameplay experience at scale. In the Game2Player loop, a Builder agent adapts existing web games, exposes their internal state, and defines tasks with state-based progress measures and success checks. A Coding Player and a VLM Player then attempt the tasks and report problems to the Builder for repair, so that play serves as both environment validation and training data collection. With Game2Player, we build 568 verified web games with 3,436 tasks, collect 15.7K trajectories (307 hours of gameplay), and hold out 50 games as the benchmark PlayerBench. To evaluate the collected experience as training data, we train VLM agents with progress-weighted SFT, assigning greater weight to steps that advance task progress. Game2Player-9B improves progress from 14.3% to 31.2% on PlayerBench and from 30.0% to 53.1% on the external GameWorld benchmark. More broadly, our work suggests a path for visual agents to scale their gameplay experience by building, verifying, and learning from existing game worlds.

title: BEV-Diffusion: Camera-Only Traversability Navigation with BEV Memory and Efficient Cross-Robot Adaptation
summary: Robot navigation requires both an understanding of the scene and an efficient adaptation to new robots, yet current methods rely on expensive LiDAR sensors, long mapping and modular pipelines. We present BEV-Diffusion, a camera-only model that learns a bird's-eye view (BEV) traversability map, its uncertainty and the path in a single network. A frozen DINOv2 backbone encodes consecutive RGB frames, which inverse perspective mapping and Bayesian fusion lift into the BEV, and a ranking loss keeps outdoor traversability graded rather than binary, separating asphalt from grass (median 0.94 vs. 0.75). On this map, a transformer denoiser generates polar waypoints in a few DDIM steps, and uncertainty-aware guidance refines the path and ends it where the map is no longer reliable. At deployment, a metric BEV memory keeps obstacles after they leave the camera view and warm starts each sample from the previous, ego-motion compensated path. Because the planner jointly learns the path, the map, and its uncertainty, it selects routes through terrain it can confidently traverse. In an unseen courtyard, a wheeled-legged robot autonomously traveled 120 m, completing 96% of the route without intervention, compared with 75-88% for the baselines. Even under low-light conditions after sunset, the proposed model completed the route without requiring any intervention. Retraining only the BEV head, about 3% of the parameters, adapts the model to a small legged robot in 2.3 min. Indoors, the memory gets this robot out of maze-like traps: it retains 62-66% of the nearby out-of-view obstacles, against at most 3% for the baselines, and the robot achieves 67-100% task progress, compared with 20-40% for the evaluated baselines.

title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
summary: Large language models are increasingly used to create stories for children. Since bedtime stories can shape children's perceptions of social roles, this raises concerns about whether LLMs adapt narrative portrayals according to the intended recipient's gender. We conducted a large-scale study to examine gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories. Using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design, we analyze 62,873 retained stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles. We introduce a multi-level evaluation framework combining context-adjusted lexical rate contrasts, relative stereotype alignment, narrator-recipient interaction analysis, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions to examine both the consistency and interpretability of these differences. Our results reveal systematic differences in narrative framing: son-directed stories emphasize higher agency and lower communion compared to daughter-directed stories. While narrator gender expresses limited moderation on these patterns, high sociability exhibits a more pronounced interaction. Human evaluations demonstrate consistent agreement, although correspondence with lexical measures varies across narrative dimensions. Additionally, hidden-state analyses reveal decodable recipient-gender information. These findings demonstrate persistent yet context-dependent representational disparities in LLM-generated children's stories and motivate narrative-specific bias evaluation beyond short-form benchmarks.

title: GenRF: Generative Registration-free Image Fusion
summary: Multi-modal image fusion combines complementary observations to improve scene visibility and perception. However, in real-world acquisition, differences in sensing principles and configurations introduce geometric discrepancies, while degradations further compromise source quality. Existing methods typically rely on explicit registration, yet large parallax complicates correspondence estimation, while mismatched fields of view leave some regions without cross-modal counterparts. Meanwhile, independent restoration underuses cross-modal information, whereas restoration-fusion methods assuming alignment remain vulnerable to misregistration. This study revisits misaligned and degraded image fusion in the era of generative foundation models, in which cross-attention enables position-agnostic complementary information aggregation, while generative priors support degradation recovery and inference in missing regions. Building on this perspective, we propose GenRF, which adapts pretrained FLUX through LoRA to jointly enhance degraded observations, infer missing cross-modal context, and fuse complementary information without explicitly estimating deformation fields. Extensive experiments on real-world infrared and visible captures show that GenRF delivers high-quality fusion directly from unregistered, degraded images without preprocessing, while improving downstream task performance under misalignment. Additional experiments demonstrate that GenRF can generalize to misaligned multi-exposure and multi-focus image fusion without task-specific fine-tuning. Project: https://linfeng-tang.github.io/GenRF.

title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
comments: 13 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 AI Measurement Science Workshop
summary: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting posterior gives exact uncertainty about the modelled success rate without numerical integration or neural inference. A public evaluation covers 79 system-benchmark pairs and eight seeds, reaching Brier ALC 0.200250 for the submitted method. Accompanying code and sufficient statistics reconstruct the fitted prior byte for byte and replay all 632 evaluation trajectories. The result demonstrates how much predictive value a compact Bayesian model can extract from sparse target feedback at very low online cost.

title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
summary: Vision-Language Models increasingly rely on textual reasoning to solve advanced multimodal tasks. Despite its effectiveness, this paradigm faces two fundamental limitations. First, relying on textual reasoning alone can limit perceptual ability in vision-centric questions, where accurate answers depend on interpreting task-relevant visual evidence. Second, applying textual reasoning uniformly across inputs overlooks question-dependent variation in both reasoning modality and depth, often producing verbose and unnecessary traces when little logical inference is required. To this end, we propose Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning (AVTR), which introduces visual imagination as a complementary reasoning modality to textual thinking, enabling the model to revisit its visual observations and distill the salient evidence through generative visual reflection. Furthermore, we formulate reasoning-modality selection as a learned routing problem, allowing a single policy to adaptively harness the complementary strengths of visual reflection and textual reasoning in response to the perceptual and inferential demands of the input. Across 16 benchmarks, AVTR improves the average score by 4.5 points over Qwen3.5 baseline, while reducing inference latency by 33\%. It also scales effectively into a smaller size backbone, outperforming the evaluated 2B-scale baselines.
